content.text: Recently, I've been under a lot of pressure at work. I watched two movies, "Little Forest" and "Our Little Sister," and I feel like my whole being has calmed down.
It sounds very soothing. I haven't seen it yet, but I'm quite interested. Could you elaborate on what specifically brings you a sense of calm?
For example, in "Our Little Sister," the scenes of the sisters living together in the old house, with the color palette of the rainy season, give me a sense of tranquility.
The atmosphere in the picture is indeed very warm, reminiscent of the relaxed feeling we had during our remote dining sessions. How has Chen Pi been lately?

It's recovering well, thanks to the PetPace app you recommended. I'm still using the weekly planner to keep track of care details. The slow, everyday moments in the movie reminded me of the poetic trivialities of taking care of Chen Pi.
Glad to hear that Chen Pi is doing better. You mentioned the movie has a slow pace—does that align with the slow living concept we discussed earlier?

Yes, just like this poster of "Our Little Sister," where the sisters sit in the courtyard, engaging in simple conversations filled with warmth. It makes me feel that even during stressful times, solace can be found in the details.
I understand how you feel, just like when I optimize algorithms, finding simple logic from complex problems. Where can I watch these movies?
It's available on both Bilibili and iQiyi. If you're interested, I can share the links.

Okay, thank you. I've been under a lot of pressure with my projects lately, so I really need this kind of relaxation. I tried the tomato and egg noodles from the healing recipes you recommended earlier, and they were very effective.
That's great! There are also many food scenes in movies, like in "Little Forest" where they grow their own vegetables and cook, and that sense of self-sufficiency really moves me.
It sounds like a form of spiritual self-sufficiency, which aligns well with the core values you pursue. I’ll make time to look into it, as it might help me optimize the balance between work and life.
And this scene of walking by the seaside, with its cool color palette, brings a sense of tranquility. Sharing these moments has also helped soothe my own emotions.

The sense of tranquility in the picture is very strong. Thank you for the recommendation; I plan to watch it this weekend. If I have any thoughts after watching, we can chat about it, just like we did during our remote dinner.
Great, I'm really looking forward to it. From the time Chen Pi fell ill until now, your support has made me feel that this kind of sharing is truly meaningful.
Likewise, your attention to detail and sense of nostalgia have taught me a lot as well. Let's stay in touch and keep sharing these healing moments.
